sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球海事商船注册旗国、借鉴特拉华州公司法的非公开发行实体

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Ownership and Cross-Border Sub-Licensing of Trademarks and Patents

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Republic of the Marshall Islands (Unitary national offshore corporate jurisdiction, Majuro registry)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid common law system; corporate statutes modeled on Delaware General Corporation Law and the US Model Business Corporation Act; customary law applies to land and traditional matters; judicial precedent from the RMI High Court and Supreme Court.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States–Republic of the Marshall Islands Tax Information Exchange Agreement (in force 2003)
Compact of Free Association with the United States (amended 2003; funding framework renewed 2023)
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER-Plus, in force 2020)
No comprehensive double taxation agreement or full bilateral investment treaty currently in force

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2013 (as amended, with the 2018 amendments implementing beneficial ownership requirements); Business Corporations Act 1990 (BCA) Sec. 21–27 (name, registered office, registered agent); RMI Financial Intelligence Unit directives and Beneficial Ownership Filing Guidance; FATF Recommendations 24–25 as transposed into national law.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the licensed RMI Registered Agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each incorporator and beneficial owner executing before a notary public in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if executed in a Hague Convention member state; otherwise Consular Legalization at the competent RMI honorary consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified notarized passport copies of all directors, officers, and UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or licensed certified accountant in the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source of Wealth and Source of Funds declaration with independent bank reference letter
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank of the UBO on original bank letterhead with certified signatures
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where available; otherwise bank attestation plus Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent registry extract for any corporate UBO at or above the 25% threshold
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country companies registry or equivalent competent authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Ownership structure chart and UBO declaration form (AML/CFT Form BO-1)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicant and UBOs certified by the licensed Registered Agent

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-acceptance screening of UBOs, directors, officers, and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN list, UK HMT, and EU CFSP financial sanctions lists, plus RMI FIU alerts and Interpol notices; mandatory enhanced due diligence for foreign and domestic politically exposed persons under the AML/CFT Act, including verified source of wealth and ongoing transaction monitoring; the licensed agent applies Medium_Risk_Enhanced treatment because the target payment rails are Swift royalty and intercompany wires; any match triggers immediate suspension, STR filing with the RMI FIU, and refusal of incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands; electronic filing exclusively through the portal administered by the Association of the Marshall Islands (AMI) on behalf of the Registrar via a licensed Registered Agent.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate register is maintained exclusively in English using Latin (Roman) script; names in ideographic or non-Roman scripts (e.g., Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic) are not accepted; a Romanized transliteration that is phonetically consistent and distinguishable in the English register is mandatory; the name must end with a corporate designator such as Corporation, Incorporated, Company, Limited, or recognized abbreviation, and must not be deceptively similar to any existing registered or reserved name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name clearance is applied through a licensed Registered Agent; if the Registrar rejects a name, the agent may file a written request for reconsideration within 15 business days identifying distinguishing elements; if the rejection is sustained, the applicant may reserve an alternative name or file an administrative appeal to the High Court of the Marshall Islands under the BCA; a successful reservation may be renewed for successive 120-day periods upon payment of the applicable renewal fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted. A non-resident Business Corporation satisfies the statutory registered-office obligation by designating the physical suite of its licensed Registered Agent in Majuro; no local employees, premises, or books are required under the BCA. However, given the pure IP HoldCo model (ISIC 6420/NAICS 533110), the OECD BEPS and EU Code of Conduct Group substance dialogue may prompt commercial counterparties and paying licensees to demand evidence of economic substance in the jurisdiction of the licensor; the RMI currently imposes no economic substance filing on non-resident BCs, and no local substance staffing is required for incorporation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for this structure: approximately 2%–3% annualized risk of an unannounced physical inspection, which is not a standard practice of the RMI Registrar for non-resident business corporations without local assets, employees, or government concessions; risk would increase materially if the company later holds RMI maritime or government-related assets.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and reservation fee (BCA Sec. 22)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Majuro (collected via AMI)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing of Articles of Incorporation (authorized capital up to USD 50,000)
UBO, PEP, and sanctions screening and AML/KYC onboarding by licensed agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Registered Agent (AMI-affiliated corporate service provider)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed Registered Agent and registered office arrangement — first annual retainer
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for non-resident Business Corporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and Apostille of the five-document KYC/UBO bundle in countries of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and designated Apostille competent authority in each origin country

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization contingency for any signatory residing in a non-Hague Apostille state
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: RMI Honorary Consulate or Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the signatory's home state

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Republic of the Marshall Islands Code (RMI Code), Title 24, Business Corporations Act (BCA), as amended - formation provisions (Articles of Incorporation), registered office and registered agent provisions, and director and officer appointment provisions
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (recorded by the Registrar; Certificate of Incorporation issued upon filing)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum authorized or paid-up share capital is required for a non-resident Business Corporation; the Board determines the consideration for issued shares, and no escrow account or capital deposit is required by the Registrar for this IP HoldCo
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, THAT the initial subscription of the Corporation's authorized capital stock by the subscribing shareholders is hereby approved; the proposed issuance of shares to each subscriber upon such consideration as the Board determines is accepted; and the Secretary is directed to record the share ledger accordingly.

RESOLVED, THAT the registered office shall be maintained at the address of the Corporation's licensed registered agent in Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands, and such agent is ratified for the statutory term as the Corporation's registered agent.

RESOLVED, THAT the following officers are elected: President, Secretary, and Treasurer, each with customary authority; and the President is authorized to open bank accounts, execute royalty and sub-license agreements, and pay all fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Availability Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands, acting through a licensed RMI registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent submits a name reservation request to the Registrar. The proposed corporate name must be distinguishable and must include the statutory suffix Corporation, Incorporated, Limited, Ltd, or an approved abbreviation. Confirm that no domestic or foreign registered entity currently holds the same or a deceptively similar name.
required_dossiers: Name reservation request form of the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as conflicting or deceptively similar, submit an alternative name or file a consent or certificate of no objection from the existing name holder; re-file within the Registrar's stated response period at no additional statutory charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator, licensed registered agent, and notary public (submission window: Office of the Registrar of Corporations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation stating the corporate name, the purpose to engage in any lawful business including ownership and cross-border sub-licensing of trademarks and patents, the registered office address in Majuro and the registered agent's name, the authorized share structure (no par value shares are customary), incorporator details, and any opt-in provisions. Execute before a notary public and deliver the original instrument to the registered agent.
required_dossiers: Consent of registered agent to serve
Proof of identity (PIC) of incorporator and initial directors/officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries an omission such as a missing signature block or defective purpose clause, execute a certificate of correction or refile amended Articles; the Registrar will preserve the requested original filing date where permitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing, Fee Payment, and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Articles of Incorporation with the Registrar together with the statutory filing fee. Pay the government filing fee for a non-resident business corporation (USD 250 standard, subject to the authorized share schedule; expedited processing is available for an additional fee). Upon recording, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and certified copies.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney or filing authorization to the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or queried for deficient content or fee shortfall, cure by paying the deficiency or filing corrected Articles within the Registrar's cure period; request expedited endorsement to maintain the original effective time where statute allows.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Initial Directors by the Incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator acting for the shareholders (internal governance action; no public filing required unless the Articles name the initial directors)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporator executes a written appointment of the initial board of directors, or the initial directors are named in the Articles. For a non-resident business corporation, directors need not be RMI residents or citizens. Each director accepts appointment in writing and provides identifying data for the corporate register.
required_dossiers: Incorporator's written consent appointing initial directors
Proof of identity (PIC) and information sheet for each director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director declines after appointment, the incorporator or the remaining directors appoint a replacement by written consent; no public filing is required for a non-resident board change.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Organizational Meeting and Adoption of Bylaws and First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting, either actually or by unanimous written consent. The Board adopts the Bylaws, approves the First Board Resolution covering share subscription and issuance, adopts the registered office and registered agent, elects the President, Secretary, and Treasurer, and authorizes the opening of bank accounts and the execution of IP license and royalty documents.
required_dossiers: Notice of organizational meeting or unanimous written consent
First Board Resolution in written consent form
Share subscription agreements and stock ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a notice or quorum defect is asserted, call a fresh meeting or obtain unanimous written consent in lieu of the meeting; ratification of prior acts is permitted in accordance with the Business Corporations Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Revenue Compliance Setup and Issuance of Certificate of Good Standing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands, and RMI revenue/treasury function (via registered agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, maintain the registered office and agent, pay the annual license fee (USD 250 per year, plus any applicable revenue or tax registration for the non-resident exempt entity), and request a Certificate of Good Standing from the Registrar for bank account opening and client due diligence purposes. Record all share issuances in the statutory ledger.
required_dossiers: Statutory share ledger and minutes book
Request letter for Certificate of Good Standing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate is withheld due to unpaid annual fees or missing annual filings, pay the arrears and any late penalty and apply for reinstatement or restored good standing before a new certificate is issued.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for the registered non-resident IP HoldCo (no physical or industrial operations in the RMI). If physical business activities commence later, the competent authority would be the Foreign Investment Business Licence (FIBL) Registrar under the Foreign Investment Business Act 2010, together with the Business Licence regime under the Business Licence Act.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating, manufacturing, or industrial permit is required for a non-resident IP licensing corporation. Contingent license if premises or employees are established: Foreign Investment Business Licence (FIBL) and an ordinary Business Licence; no manufacturing permit applies because no production is carried out.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA), Republic of the Marshall Islands
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - a pure patent and trademark licensing HoldCo has no physical project, construction, or discharge in RMI territory; no EIA registration or report is triggered under the RMI Environment Impact Assessment Act. Contingent classification: Category II (screening) or Category III (full EIA) if any physical office, data center, or manufacturing facility is later established.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not triggered - zero wastewater, VOC, and solid waste outputs arise from the licensing activity. If a physical facility is later opened, compliance with EPA wastewater standards, solid and hazardous waste regulations, and marine pollution prevention (MARPOL / protected lagoon) requirements for Majuro or Ebeye would apply, including EPA-approved waste hauling documentation for office-generated waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable - no physical workplace, employees, or fire-risk premises in the RMI. If a future office is staffed, required clearances would include a fire safety certification from the RMI Fire Services, structural and load inspection under the building permitting authority, and an Occupational Safety and Health clearance under RMI OSH regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Revenue and Taxation Office, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Majuro Atoll, MH; corporate-status filings are administered by the RMI Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro, exclusively through RMI-licensed registered agents. There is no national online tax-filing portal; GRT registrations and returns are accepted in paper form through the Revenue and Taxation Office.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: A foreign-owned entity incorporates under the Business Corporations Act 1990 by filing Articles of Incorporation through an RMI-licensed registered agent and receives a Certificate of Incorporation with a corporate registration number. Step 2: The directors execute a sworn non-resident declaration and the corporation is issued a Certificate of Non-Resident Domestic Status confirming that no business will be conducted within the Republic. Step 3: Because the RMI imposes no corporate income tax, no income-tax TIN is issued; the Non-Resident Domestic Certificate is the operative tax-identity instrument. Step 4: A Gross Revenue Tax account number (the functional taxpayer ID) is obtained only if the corporation subsequently undertakes business activity inside the Republic; otherwise no GRT registration is made. Step 5: Patents and trademarks may be recorded with the RMI Registrar of Patents and Trademarks for evidentiary strengthening, but such recording is not a tax-registration requirement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: a Non-Resident Domestic Business Corporation is categorically exempt from all RMI national taxation (no corporate income tax, no gross revenue tax, no business license tax, no withholding tax on outbound royalties or dividends) provided it derives no RMI-source revenue and conducts no business within the Republic. Territorial scope confines taxation exclusively to locally sourced activity; no RMI permanent-establishment or substance filing is required for the exempt status.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or income-tax classification election exists because the Republic levies no corporate income tax. Available statutory elections: (i) Non-Resident Domestic Corporation exemption election under the Business Corporations Act, evidenced by a Registrar-issued certificate and sworn affidavit; (ii) elective small-business GRT exemptions for de minimis local revenues; and (iii) foreign-registered non-resident corporation status, which likewise avoids RMI taxation. The RMI has not enacted hybrid-mismatch, CFC, OECD BEPS, or Pillar Two election rules; no substance-based carve-out filings apply.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Gross Revenue Tax (GRT) - a sales-type gross-receipts tax under the Gross Revenue Tax Act; the RMI has no VAT, no GST, and no separate sales-and-use tax. The standard statutory GRT rate for general business is 3%; insurance, banking, utilities, and fuel carry separate schedules. Non-resident IP HoldCos with no RMI nexus bear an effective 0% rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold in USD: GRT registration is nexus-triggered rather than turnover-triggered. Any person engaged in a business activity within the Republic must obtain a business license and GRT account; a non-resident Domestic Corporation without RMI-source gross revenue is outside the tax base and is not permitted or required to register. De minimis exemptions apply to very small local businesses (statutory schedules around USD 5,000-10,000 of annual gross revenue), but these exemptions are irrelevant to non-resident cross-border IP licensing.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. The RMI has not implemented electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, API-based e-filing, or digital stamping. GRT returns are filed on paper (annual or periodic) with the Revenue and Taxation Office; no fiscal-data interface exists for wire-based royalty payments or intercompany SWIFT transfers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The GRT applies only to gross revenue derived from business conducted in the Republic. Cross-border outbound licensing of patents and trademarks to non-RMI licensees, with royalties remitted by SWIFT wire from abroad, is excluded from the RMI tax base by the territorial sourcing rule; no 0% VAT claim, input-credit mechanism, or refund application is required. The exclusion is automatic and self-executing provided that: (i) all licensing counterparties are non-residents; (ii) no negotiation, sub-licensing, or management activities are performed from an RMI office; and (iii) the corporation maintains its current Non-Resident Domestic Certificate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration - required only where goods accompany a transaction; not applicable to pure intangible patent/trademark licensing.
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill - not applicable to cross-border IP sub-licensing; retained only where goods are the physical delivery channel.
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 trace evidencing the foreign-sourced royalty inflow.
Non-Resident Domestic Corporation Tax Exemption Certificate together with the executed license agreement and royalty schedule as the operative substantiation package for GRT exclusion.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Revenue and Taxation Office may reopen assessments within the statutory window (typically three years; extended where fraud or material omission is shown) and claw back GRT wherever the exemption condition is breached, e.g., an RMI resident licensee, local contracting activity, or directors conducting board/management functions inside the Republic. Consequences include reclassification as a resident taxpayer, mandatory registration and payment of 3% GRT on all RMI-source gross revenue, monthly interest on deficiencies (approximately 1% per month or pro rata), late-filing penalties of 5% per month up to 25%, fraud and willful-neglect penalties of up to 25% of the underpayment, and cancellation of the Non-Resident Domestic Certificate. In egregious cases, uncollected tax can be recovered from directors, and the corporation may be struck from the RMI register. The RMI imposes no exchange-control fines because no statutory repatriation obligations exist.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank: None. The Republic of the Marshall Islands has no domestic central bank and no independent exchange-control authority. Legal tender is the United States dollar. Banking and AML/CFT supervision is exercised by the Marshall Islands Banking Commissioner within the Ministry of Finance under the Banking Act 1991; USD clearing is ultimately settled through the U.S. Federal Reserve correspondent system.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility for both current and capital account items. The RMI maintains no exchange controls, no surrender requirements, no approval regime for inbound or outbound payments, and no distinction between authorised and unauthorised dealers. Profit remittance and royalty outflows are not subject to RMI withholding tax or remittance tax. The principal practical hurdles are source-country withholding taxes on IP royalties, particularly where the MH BC lacks a double-tax-treaty or treaty-tie benefit, and the need to document economic substance to satisfy banking and tax-transparency counterparties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. There is no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no requirement to repatriate or surrender export proceeds or intellectual-property license fees to a designated bank. The MH BC may retain export and royalty receipts in USD indefinitely in any bank account, and may freely disburse them for working capital, IP acquisition, dividends, management fees, or intercompany settlement without central bank approval.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Guam - Marshall Islands Branch
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD Account / Treasury Clearing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. The RMI does not maintain a statutory fintech EMI licensing category or a Regulatory Sandbox. Offshore digital EMI platforms are not automatically recognised as banks or money transmitters under the Banking Act, and global EMIs typically classify the RMI as a high-risk correspondent jurisdiction. An offshore EMI may be used only as a supplementary collections rail for small non-USD receipts if the EMI's terms expressly permit RMI-licensed non-resident corporations, but it cannot replace a physical bank relationship. All treasury liquidity must be swept into an RMI-licensed bank or a U.S. correspondent account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for directors, authorized signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners of a non-resident Business Corporation opening a new account at Bank of Marshall Islands; fully remote opening is not available as the standard route. Bank of Guam may accept a remote interview only when supported by an existing client relationship, apostilled corporate documents, and notarized KYC forms verified by a recognized bank officer or U.S. notary; in practice, a physical meeting at a branch or at an RMI/U.S. government office remains safest. Original corporate resolutions, certificate of good standing, registered-agent letter, passport copies, and proof of residential address must be provided.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore IP Holding Company incorporated in the RMI with no visible local substance and no local tax file.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Good Standing issued by the RMI Registrar; registered agent certificate; notarized current corporate bylaws; board minutes demonstrating actual management of IP assets; executed office lease or service arrangement in Majuro; economic-substance narrative mapping IP ownership, sub-licensing decisions, and treasury functions; non-resident tax exemption statement under the Business Corporation Act.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Obscure beneficial ownership chain using nominees, bearer-share history, or multiple intermediate entity layers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified UBO register with all individuals owning 10% or more; full legal-entity ownership chart from ultimate parent to MH BC; passport copies and proof of residential address for each UBO; source of wealth and source of funds statements; bank references from the parent company's bank; sworn declarations from the registered agent confirming no bearer shares.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Royalty-income and sublicensing cash flows showing thin margins or round-tripping between group entities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed trademark or patent license agreements with commercial terms; patent and trademark registration certificates; royalty calculation files using CUP or transactional net-margin benchmarking under OECD transfer-pricing principles; audited financial statements of the MH BC; intercompany invoices and utilization reports; group transfer-pricing policy; projected cash-flow model demonstrating commercial purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty funds originating from patent assertion entities, litigation settlements, or high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions-list and PEP screening results for all counterparties; adverse-media search report; underlying licensing or settlement agreements with legal opinions; KYC questionnaire of each licensee; board resolution approving the commercial rationale; case-by-case AML risk assessment and enhanced monitoring plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Vague payment narratives using 'general remittance' or unformatted SWIFT remarks masking IP royalties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoices or credit notes; license utilization reports from sub-licensees; tax invoices where applicable; SWIFT payment instructions using a standardized 'Royalty and License Fee' purpose-code mapping; complete population of SWIFT field 70 with invoice and license identifiers; transaction-monitoring trail and monthly reconciliation to the licensing register.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity contributions from the ultimate parent to the MH BC should be executed by SWIFT MT103 in USD, cleared through the corresponding U.S. Fedwire or CHIPS correspondent network. The remittance must use a precise purpose-code mapping for direct investment / equity capital, with the MH BC's bank account as beneficiary and the company name stated exactly as 'MH_BC'. The payment reference line should contain 'CAPITAL INJECTION - SHARE ISSUANCE - MH_BC' plus the related share resolution number. The bank must receive the board resolution authorizing issuance, shareholder subscription agreement, updated share register, source-of-funds evidence for the originating shareholder, and certification that the capital injection is not for tax evasion. Amounts in excess of the RMI/U.S. reporting threshold may be reported as currency transactions; this does not restrict the inflow but requires accurate recording.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound royalty and licence-fee settlements should be routed over SWIFT MT103 in USD, either direct or via an MT202 COV correspondent-cover instruction. For larger trade-linked licensing transactions, an irrevocable documentary commercial letter of credit is permissible: the MH BC or its bank issues an MT700 LC under UCP600, with the beneficiary bank, and settlement occurs by sight or deferred draft after presentation of the commercial invoice, license utilization certificate, proof of IP registration, and shipping or milestone documents where applicable. All outbound payments must include the relevant licence contract reference, invoice number, and a purpose code reflecting 'charges for the use of intellectual property' rather than a generic remittance, and must pass risk-based sanctions screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards in USD/EUR, USD/GBP, USD/JPY and other freely convertible currencies against projected royalty receivables
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted-convertibility currencies such as CNY, INR, IDR, or KRW where the underlying exposure is a contractual licensee payment obligation
FX swaps to convert non-USD royalty receipts into USD on a matched spot-forward basis
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for simultaneous FX and interest-rate hedging on intercompany IP acquisition debt or structured receivables
European-style FX options purchased for hedge-only purposes, documented under an ISDA Master Agreement, with the underlying license exposure evidenced to the bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporation Report and Franchise Tax Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, RMI Business Registry, Office of the Attorney General
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of the calendar month immediately preceding the incorporation anniversary month, filed annually
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of USD 200 plus USD 50 per commenced month of default; company marked not in good standing on the register; failure to cure within 90 days after written notice triggers administrative dissolution or strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed on a non-resident Business Corporation unless a court or shareholders holding at least 10% of issued shares demand an independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or US GAAP as acceptable frameworks for records prepared under the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act; no public filing of financial statements is required for a non-resident exempt company.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Marshall Islands has no separate public UBO return; however, the Board must maintain accurate share transfer records in the company's minute book, and the annual corporation report must state directors, officers, registered agent, and registered office information.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 - USD 1,200 per year depending on service provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable as audit is voluntary; if voluntarily prepared, USD 2,500 - USD 5,000 for a simple IP holding company

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% effective rate for a Non-Resident Business Corporation (BC); the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) Income Tax Act (Title 54, RMI Code) taxes only income sourced within the RMI, and a BC holding valid non-resident status under the Business Corporations Act (BCA) is outside the charge. A 3% gross-receipts analogue applies only to entities actually engaged in business within the RMI; the scope entity has no RMI-source income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory non-resident exemption: no corporate income tax, no capital gains tax, no dividend or interest withholding tax, no royalty withholding tax, no gross receipts tax, no VAT or goods-and-services tax, and no payroll tax for non-resident officers. Recurring cost base consists solely of the annual Registrar fee (US$125 minimum tier, scaling by authorized share capital), the licensed registered agent retainer, and any CRS/AML compliance service fees.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_regime_note: Not applicable: the non-resident BC has no RMI tax base, so no loss computation, carryforward, or carryback arises. Any reference to loss utilization is moot in the RMI itself; loss-pooling considerations are relevant only in the licensor's foreign parent jurisdiction.
corporate_income_tax_regime.territoriality_and_source_rules: RMI taxation follows source-based territoriality: income attributable to activities performed or property located within the RMI is the only taxable subject. The licensing of patents and trademarks for use entirely outside the RMI, with payments made offshore, creates no RMI nexus. The BC must merely avoid physical office, employees, or contract performance in the RMI to preserve the exemption.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form BC-AR1 (Annual Report and Registered Agent Certification), filed through the RMI Registrar of Corporations Electronic Filing Portal; filing is performed by the licensed RMI registered agent, with corporate records maintained at the agent's Majuro address.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 60 days after the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year BC, no later than 1 March of the following year. The fiscal year end is fixed by the board on first filing and governs all subsequent filings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Corporate Name and File Number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact registered legal name and the unique file number assigned by the Registrar at incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the name exactly as issued; no trade-name or DBA deviations are permitted on the annual report.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name of the licensed RMI registered agent and its physical street address in Majuro, RMI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The agent must be a licensed registered-agent entity; a PO Box alone is insufficient and will trigger rejection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names, nationalities, and residential addresses of all directors and officers, including the secretary and authorized signatories.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident natural persons may serve in all capacities; the form requires actual residential addresses, not post-office aliases.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Number of authorized shares, par value (if any), number of issued shares, and aggregate consideration received.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The minimum capital requirement is zero; however, the issued capitalization should be commercially aligned with the patent-licensing portfolio valuation to avoid sham-entity challenges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Narrative description of the entity's actual business purpose.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 'Ownership and cross-border licensing of patents and trademarks' (ISIC 6420); do not use generic 'investment holding' wording if the actual asset base is IP.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of every individual who directly or indirectly owns or controls more than 25% of the shares or voting rights, or who exercises control via other means.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The register of beneficial owners must be physically available at the registered agent's office for inspection by the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit; updates must be filed within 30 days of any change.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certification that the corporation has conducted no business within the RMI, derived no RMI-source income, and holds no RMI-situs real property or assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The declaration preserves the zero-tax status. Falsification is a criminal statutory-fraud offense and forfeits the corporate veil.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late fee equal to 10% of the annual report fee per commenced month of delinquency, subject to a cap of the annual fee; failure to file for two consecutive years leads to administrative strike-off by the Registrar. Continued non-payment or non-appointment of a registered agent causes automatic dissolution; directors and officers remain jointly liable for debts incurred after dissolution and for unpaid Registrar fees.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: RMI Income Tax Return (Mirror U.S. Form 1040/1120 architecture) - Not Required for the Exempt Non-Resident BC; an RMI Tax Clearance Certificate (TCC) may be voluntarily requested from the RMI Revenue and Taxation Division when the BC's foreign payor counterparties demand proof of exempt status.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (only upon Revenue demand; no standing filing obligation)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No return is due by default. If the Revenue and Taxation Division issues a notice asserting RMI-source income, a written response and return must be submitted within 30 days of the notice date or by the date stated in the notice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross income derived from sources within the RMI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter zero where all royalty streams arise from licenses over foreign-registered patents and are paid by non-resident licensees into an offshore account.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses directly attributable to RMI-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 'N/A'; no deduction schedule is needed in the absence of RMI-source gross income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RMI-source gross income less attributable deductions.
3% gross-basis tax on fees paid to non-residents for services physically performed in the RMI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable to royalty income; however, any separately invoiced technical-support fees rendered from within the RMI would be captured here.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: No penalty for non-filing where no return is due; any taxpayer that receives a notice and fails to respond faces an administrative assessment equal to 100% of the asserted RMI-source gross income at the 3% rate, plus a 25% delinquency penalty and monthly interest of 1%. Willful evasion carries a fine up to US$50,000 under the RMI Criminal Code.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - the RMI imposes no withholding tax on dividends, distributions, or deemed distributions made by a non-resident BC. The BC also has no obligation to report dividend payments to the RMI Revenue and Taxation Division.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The RMI has no comprehensive double taxation agreement (DTA) network and does not issue conventional tax-residency certificates. Consequently, treaty relief is unavailable and unnecessary: the domestic statutory rate is already zero. Protocol for foreign payor due diligence: (1) obtain an RMI Certificate of Good Standing from the Registrar of Corporations; (2) obtain an RMI Tax Clearance Certificate from the Revenue and Taxation Division confirming the non-resident exemption; (3) prepare a legal opinion citing Section 17 of the BCA and the territorial-source rule of Title 54 RMI Code; and (4) deliver the package through the registered agent when the foreign counterparty's tax authority requests documentary proof for foreign tax credit or DTA purposes.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory 0% on patent/trademark royalties and on debt interest paid by the BC to both residents and non-residents. The RMI levies no interest equalization tax, no capital duty, and no financial-transactions tax. The separate 3% Non-Resident Services Tax applies only to fees for services physically performed inside the RMI; pure IP royalty remittances and loan interest paid by the BC into offshore accounts fall outside that gross-basis charge. The BC should nonetheless include a governing-law clause in each license stating that payments are consideration for the right to use IP outside the RMI.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: None - the RMI has not enacted transfer-pricing legislation and prescribes no Local File, Master File, or Country-by-Country Reporting thresholds. Because the BC is tax-exempt, there is no RMI taxable baseline against which an adjustment could be imposed. Practical threshold for the group: where the BC is the ultimate IP owner in a multinational chain and its parent jurisdiction applies CbC reporting, the group must document a demonstrable arm's-length royalty rate to defend against the parent jurisdiction's controlled-foreign-company (CFC) and anti-avoidance rules; there is no local-currency threshold, so the relevant thresholds are those of the foreign taxing jurisdictions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_comment: Although the RMI does not mandate TP files, the BC should maintain a contemporaneous transfer-pricing memorandum covering: (i) the legal chain of title for each patent/trademark; (ii) the benchmarked royalty rate using CUP or TNMM based on a royalty-rate database; (iii) the functions, assets, and risks of the BC (limited holding and licensing administration); (iv) the commercial rationale for price adjustments; and (v) board minutes approving each license and intercompany agreement. Absence of these documents will be used by foreign tax authorities to recharacterize the BC as a conduit.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The RMI has not enacted BVI/Cayman-style Economic Substance Regulations. However, two substance-related obligations apply: (1) the BCA and the Registered Agents Licensing Act require a licensed RMI registered agent, a physical registered office, and a beneficial ownership register - these constitute the minimum legal substance; and (2) the RMI's participation in the OECD global tax transparency framework (CRS and exchange of information upon request) means that foreign tax authorities will treat the RMI entity's lack of commercial substance as a red flag. The BC should demonstrably: hold legal title to registered IP; maintain board minutes and license agreements in execution form; use a bank account opened in the name of the BC; and ensure cash flows are not circular or pre-funded by the operating licensee.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Executing backdated or fictitious patent license agreements under which royalties are paid by a high-tax foreign operating entity to the BC without legal title in the BC, without board authorization, without actual enforcement of the license, or with circular return of the royalty funds to the originator as loans, share capital, or management fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Foreign tax authorities will disregard the BC and reassess the royalty payer under anti-avoidance rules, imposing gross-up penalties of 20%-40% and interest. Within the RMI, willful filing of false documents or knowing participation in a fraudulent scheme violates Section 5.08 of the RMI Criminal Code, punishable by a fine up to US$50,000 and/or imprisonment up to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who orchestrate sham licensing are jointly and severally liable for the foreign tax restitution; they may face civil asset forfeiture, travel bans issued by foreign courts in MLA proceedings, director-disqualification orders, and extradition requests predicated on tax evasion or wire fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The BC holds no registered patents, maintains no license contracts, has no bank account, is administered purely by the registered agent with zero board activity, and is used solely to hold funds or invoices; the IP portfolio is owned and controlled by the foreign parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the RMI Business Corporations Act, the Registrar may strike off the entity for non-filing or for failure to maintain a registered agent, resulting in automatic dissolution and forfeiture of all statutory powers. The entity then loses its zero-tax status for practical purposes and cannot rely on RMI law to enforce contracts; foreign CFC and substance rules will tax the deemed royalty income in the parent's jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who continue to trade after strike-off are personally liable for all debts and obligations incurred; the corporate veil is pierced, exposing directors to civil restitution by creditors and by foreign revenue authorities for the full amount of diverted profits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain a current beneficial ownership register at the registered agent's office, failure to file beneficial-ownership changes within 30 days, absence of an AML/CFT risk assessment covering royalty wire flows, failure to submit Suspicious Transaction Reports to the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit, or concealment of the ultimate beneficial owner behind nominee layers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the RMI Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) Act, the entity is subject to fines up to US$250,000, freezing orders, and revocation of the registered agent's license; the Registrar may also strike off the entity for regulatory non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the designated AML officer face personal financial penalties, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 5 years where the royalty network is used to launder proceeds of foreign tax evasion or corruption; personal assets may be confiscated under the Proceeds of Crime framework.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Annual Declaration / Fraud on the Registrar
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Falsely certifying non-resident exempt status while the BC actually derives RMI-source income, or knowingly submitting false information in the annual report concerning share capital, directors, or beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A fine of US$10,000 to US$25,000 per false filing, forfeiture of the limited-liability shield, and administrative removal from the Register; the Registrar may also refer the matter for criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign a false declaration are personally liable for civil restitution of any unpaid RMI taxes (3% gross receipts plus penalties) and for third-party losses; imprisonment up to 3 years applies for false statutory declarations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany royalty rates with no benchmark, using expense-pass-through arrangements that strip all profit from the foreign operating entity, or converting equity returns into tax-deductible royalties where the BC bears no economic risk and provides no funding or services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The RMI itself imposes no TP adjustment, but the affected foreign jurisdiction will recharacterize the payments as distributions, impose withholding tax on the grossed-up amount, and apply penalties of 20%-40% plus interest; the BC's bank may terminate correspondent relationships for unusual circular flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foreign tax authorities may pursue directors personally for penalties where the director approved the pricing and knew the arrangement lacked commercial substance; this can include civil restitution of avoided taxes and travel bans pending resolution of the tax dispute.

nexus_governance_and_compliance_calendar.monthly_or_quarterly_obligations: None under RMI tax law; any ongoing obligation is contractual (e.g., bank KYC updates, license compliance reviews).
nexus_governance_and_compliance_calendar.annual_obligation_summary: BC-AR1 Annual Report due within 60 days of fiscal year-end (by 1 March for calendar year); annual registered agent fee; annual beneficial-ownership confirmation; and any voluntary TCC renewal.
nexus_governance_and_compliance_calendar.record_retention_obligation: Books and records sufficient to explain the BC's royalty transactions must be kept at the registered agent's office or a location designated in the annual report; the RMI Registrar and FIU may demand production within a prescribed period, and foreign tax authorities may obtain the records via exchange of information.

primary_statutes: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act (Title 23, RMI Code)
Registered Agents Licensing Act (Title 51A, RMI Code)
administrative_authorities: RMI Revenue and Taxation Division, Ministry of Finance
